decisions.reason: A decorative carpet close to the core range costs little to keep listed, and one year of results has not yet shown whether its value will be realized, so the option is worth holding.
A premium hand-knotted wool silk carpet fits the craftsmanship positioning, and with demand still uncertain and little cost to carry, it is worth keeping.
Several similar carpets overlap in a broad portfolio, but there is no evidence yet that this one has failed, and keeping it costs little.
The corner bench extends the established seating offer into contract and hospitality projects, and its prospects remain open while it costs little to carry.
This low-pile carpet is a cheap option to hold in a crowded carpet line, and pruning is premature before its sales results become clear.
A swivel shell chair is close to the core offer and serves both residential and workplace markets, so it is a valuable option whose uncertainty has not yet been resolved.
